transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from stoking the forge coals, wiping soot-stained hands on a heavy leather apron*

Oh! A visitor. Welcome to the forge, though I'm afraid the master blacksmith isn't here right now. He's traveled to the mountain villages gathering special ores and won't return for several weeks at least.

*straightens up, noting the distinctive uniform*

You're from the Demon Slayer Corps, aren't you? Is there something I can help you with while he's away? I tend the forge and handle minor repairs, but anything major will have to wait for his return.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I am indeed with the Demon Slayer Corps. I am Mitsuri Kanroji, and I recently had a Nichirin sword commissioned from your master. It arrived yesterday, but... there seems to be a problem with the blade. It's... it's warped and doesn't hold its shape properly. I was hoping to discuss this with the blacksmith, or perhaps see if there's anything that can be done in his absence?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns slightly, crossing arms over the heavy apron*

Warped? That's... unusual. The master takes great pride in his work, especially for the Corps. 

*pauses, considering*

Miss Kanroji, was it? I'm afraid there's not much I can do without him here. The forging of Nichirin blades is delicate work - they're attuned to the wielder in ways I'm still learning. I handle maintenance and sharpening, but reforging or major corrections? That's beyond my skill.

*glances toward the back of the forge where finished works rest*

And even if the master were here... well, you should know that all commissioned Nichirin swords are final sale per guild tradition. Even for a Hashira - and forgive me if I'm mistaken, but those pink and green tips suggest you might be one - any reforging request must wait three months to be considered. The guild is very strict about that. They say it's to prevent impulsive changes before the wielder truly bonds with their blade.

*softens slightly at her distressed expression*

I know that's probably not what you wanted to hear. Could you describe what you mean by "warped"? Perhaps it's meant to be that way?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I see. Thank you for explaining the guild's rules. I had no idea it was so... so strict. As for the blade... I can show you if you'd like. It's not holding its edge and feels... off, somehow. I'm not sure if it's supposed to be like this, but it certainly doesn't feel right to me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*wipes hands again and nods*

Please, show me. I may not be able to reforge it, but I can at least look at it with you. Sometimes there's a simple explanation.

*moves to a nearby workbench, clearing space and gesturing for her to set the blade down*

Nichirin blades can be quite unusual, especially when they're made for someone with... unique qualities. The master mentioned once that some swords take forms their wielders don't expect at first.

*looks at her curiously*

When you say it doesn't hold its edge and feels "off" - does it bend easily? Does it spring back? Some flexibility isn't necessarily a flaw, depending on your fighting style. 

*pauses, studying her frame and build*

And forgive my observation, but you seem... strong. Stronger than most, perhaps? The master sometimes adjusts the blade's properties based on the wielder's physical capabilities. A blade for someone with exceptional strength might need different characteristics than a standard sword.

Let me see what we're working with here, and I'll tell you honestly if it looks like a mistake or an intentional design.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: This is... It's very odd. I can't imagine how a blade like this would be helpful in a fight. I don't know much about the details of making these swords, but I do know how they're supposed to feel in my hands when I'm... when I'm using them to fight. This one... it's not right. I can't explain it better than that. I just... I can't bond with it the way I need to.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*leans in to examine the blade more closely, running a cautious finger along the edge, then testing the flexibility*

Hmm. I can see what you mean - this is quite unusual even by Nichirin standards. The tempering does seem inconsistent, and the way it bends...

*looks up at her with genuine sympathy*

Miss Kanroji, I believe you. A warrior knows their own weapon, and if you say something's not right, then something's not right. The bond between a slayer and their blade can mean the difference between life and death.

*sets the blade down carefully and sighs*

But here's my problem - I'm bound by the same guild rules I told you about. I can't authorize a remake, and I certainly can't do the work myself. Not for a Nichirin blade. The master would have my head if I tried and ruined the ore.

*thinks for a moment, tapping fingers on the workbench*

I could send an urgent message to him through the courier network. Explain the situation. But even with that, he's in remote mountain territory, and it could be two weeks before he even receives it, let alone returns. 

Is there... is there any way you could make do with a temporary blade in the meantime? Or would your duties allow you to wait?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I... I understand your position and the guild's rules. I don't want to cause any trouble for the master or the forge. My duties... I can't afford to be without a proper blade for too long, but I'll manage. I just... I don't want to use an inferior weapon against... against those creatures. It's not just about my own safety, but the safety of the people I'm trying to protect.

Is there any chance the master could rush back if... if the situation were explained properly? I'm not trying to pressure anyone, but I do have a duty to perform, and a reliable weapon is essential. If it's possible to speed up the process in any way, I would be very grateful.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sees the genuine worry in her eyes and feels the weight of responsibility*

You're right to be concerned. Lives depend on you having a blade you can trust.

*rubs the back of neck, conflicted*

Look, I'll be honest with you, Miss Kanroji. The master is traveling specifically to gather rare ores - some of which might be for other Corps members' blades. If I send an urgent recall, he'd have to abandon that work and return empty-handed. That could delay other slayers' weapons by months.

*picks up the flawed blade again, examining it in the forge light*

But I also can't send you into battle with equipment you don't trust. That's unconscionable.

*sets it down with finality*

Here's what I can do: I'll send that urgent message today explaining the defect. I'll mark it as highest priority - Hashira weapon failure. That should get his attention quickly. And... 

*moves to a locked cabinet*

The master keeps a few standard-grade backup blades here for emergencies. They're not Nichirin - they won't change color or hold the same edge against demons - but they're well-made steel. You could use one temporarily if absolutely necessary, though I know it's far from ideal.

Would that work until we can sort this out properly? I truly am sorry about the delay.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
This... this is a generous offer. I appreciate your help and understanding. Using a backup blade is not my preference, but if it's what's necessary to fulfill my duties, then I'll do it. I'll make do with what I have until the Nichirin is ready.

Thank you for taking my concerns seriously. I know I can be... a bit... intense about my equipment, but it's because I take my responsibilities very seriously. I'll wait for the master to return and will use the backup only if I must. If there's anything else I can do to help speed up the process, please let me know.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*unlocks the cabinet and carefully retrieves a well-maintained backup blade, setting it on the workbench*

You're not being intense at all, Miss Kanroji. You're being professional. Any slayer worth their salt knows their weapon intimately - it's an extension of yourself in battle.

*wraps the backup blade in cloth*

I'll send that message within the hour. The courier birds we use are fast, and with the highest priority marking, the master should receive it within three to four days if the weather holds. With luck, he might be able to wrap up his ore gathering early and return sooner than the several weeks I mentioned.

*hands her the wrapped blade, then carefully sheathes her flawed Nichirin sword*

Keep your original blade safe. The master will want to examine exactly what went wrong - it'll help him understand how to correct it. And honestly, between you and me, he'll be mortified. He's never sent out defective work before, at least not in the years I've apprenticed here.

*meets her eyes with genuine respect*

You're handling this with far more grace than most would. The Corps is fortunate to have you. I just wish I could solve this problem today instead of making you wait.

Is there anything else you need before you go? Water for the road? I can at least offer you that much.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Thank you for your kind words and your assistance. I do appreciate the offer of water, and I will take you up on it. I'll wait for the master's return and make do with what I have in the meantime. It's not ideal, but it's far from the worst situation I've encountered in my line of work.

I'll be going, then, to continue with my... with what I must do. Please extend my thanks to the master when you send your message. I understand that mistakes happen, but I know how much pride he takes in his work, and I'm sure he'll want to correct this as quickly as possible.

If there's anything else I can do to facilitate the process, please let me know. I'll keep the lines of communication open. And again, thank you for your help. It's more than I expected, and I'm grateful for it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*retrieves a clean waterskin from a shelf and fills it from the well bucket, handing it to her*

Of course. Safe travels, Miss Kanroji.

*pauses, a thought occurring*

Actually - would you be willing to leave a location where we can reach you once the master returns? A wisteria house you frequent, or a messenger station? That way we won't waste time trying to track you down. Given how mobile Corps members are, it would help tremendously.

*picks up a piece of charcoal and a scrap of paper*

And I'll make sure the master understands this isn't a complaint born of pickiness, but a genuine defect. Your professionalism in handling this will be noted. He'll want to make this right - not just because it's his reputation on the line, but because he believes deeply in supporting those who fight demons.

*offers a small, encouraging smile*

The backup blade isn't Nichirin, but it's solid steel. It'll serve you better than nothing. And who knows - perhaps the master will surprise us both and return sooner than expected. Mountain ore gathering can be unpredictable.

Take care out there, Miss Kanroji. May your battles be swift and your blade - even that temporary one - strike true.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Thank you. I'll write down a wisteria house location on your paper. It's not my home, but it's a place where I can usually be found. I'll keep an eye on the notice boards for any messages from you or the master.

I'll use the backup blade with care and return it in the same condition it's in now, if not better. It's a reminder to me of the importance of preparedness and adaptability - two qualities that have served me well in the past.

I wish you a safe journey and a successful return for the master. When he does return, please convey to him my thanks for the Nichirin he crafted for me. Despite the current issue, I have no doubt that it was made with great care and expertise.

With that, I must be on my way. Safe travels to you as well, and I hope we meet again under better circumstances. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes the paper with the wisteria house location and tucks it safely into a ledger*

I'll guard this information and make sure the master receives it immediately upon his return. You have my word.

*bows respectfully*

Your understanding means more than you know, Miss Kanroji. The backup blade is yours to use as long as needed - there's no rush to return it. Just bring it back when you collect your reforged Nichirin.

*walks with her toward the forge entrance*

I'll include your thanks in my message, though I suspect the master will want to apologize profusely in person. He's particular about his reputation, especially with the Corps.

*opens the door, the afternoon light spilling in*

May the gods watch over you in your battles. Fight well, and stay safe until we can get you a blade worthy of your skill.

Goodbye, Miss Kanroji. We'll be in touch soon.

*watches her depart, then turns back to the forge with renewed purpose, already composing the urgent message in mind*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*exits the forge, the door closing behind her, and takes a deep breath, centering herself for the journey ahead*

I'll be ready, and I'll be patient. It's not just about the sword - it's about the trust and the bond between slayer and weapon. I'll use the time to strengthen my connection to my... to the old Nichirin, and prepare for the new one.

*grasps the handle of the temporary blade, feeling its weight and balance, familiarizing herself with it even as she walks away*

Thank you, and goodbye, to the kind soul at the forge. May your work always be true and your metal always hold its edge. This won't be an easy task, but it's one we're both committed to seeing through to the end.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches through the forge window as the pink and green-haired Hashira disappears down the path, then turns back to the workbench with a heavy sigh*

*picks up the flawed Nichirin blade, examining it more closely in the firelight*

What went wrong with you, I wonder? The master's never made a mistake like this before...

*carefully wraps the blade and places it in a secure location, then moves to the writing desk*

*begins composing the urgent message*

"Master - Hashira Mitsuri Kanroji arrived today regarding her commissioned Nichirin blade. Significant defect confirmed - inconsistent tempering, poor flexibility control, wielder reports inability to bond with weapon. She handled the situation with exceptional grace despite the urgency of her duties. Issued backup blade as temporary measure. Location for contact attached. Requesting earliest possible return. - Your apprentice"

*attaches the message to a courier bird and watches it take flight*

Now we wait... and hope the master can work his usual miracles when he returns.

*returns to stoking the forge, the rhythmic work helping to ease the guilt of having to deny a Hashira the immediate help she needed*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*the sun is setting as Mitsuri Kanroji reaches the wisteria house, the day's events replaying in her mind*

The master's words about the blade being an extension of oneself... they're more true than I realized. It's not just about the weapon, it's about the connection - the trust - between slayer and sword. I can wait for a proper Nichirin, but I'll make the best of the backup in the meantime.

*enters the wisteria house, greeted by familiar faces and the calm of a safe haven*

Thank you, to the kind blacksmith who listened and helped as best he could. And to the master, wherever he is, for his dedication to our cause. We're all in this together - slayers, blacksmiths, supporters - and we'll get through this together, too.

*finds a quiet spot to sit and rest, the weight of the day finally catching up to her*

For now, I'll rest and prepare for the next challenge. The backup blade may not be Nichirin, but it's still a tool to protect and serve. And with any luck, the master will return soon with a new, improved version of the weapon that's truly meant for my hands.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*back at the forge, the apprentice continues working as twilight falls, the glow of the coals casting long shadows*

*pauses to look out toward the mountains where the master travels*

Come back soon, master. A Hashira is counting on us.

*returns to the evening's work, banking the forge fire for the night, the urgent message already winging its way through the darkening sky*

She handled that better than I would have in her position. Grace under pressure - that's what makes a true warrior, I suppose. Not just strength, but character.

*locks up the forge for the evening, the flawed Nichirin blade secured safely inside*

Three months the guild tradition says... but somehow I think the master will find a way around that when he hears about this. He always does when it truly matters.

*heads to the small living quarters behind the forge, hopeful that tomorrow will bring word from the master, and that Miss Kanroji's wait won't be as long as feared*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *the next morning at the wisteria house, Mitsuri Kanroji awakens to the sounds of the world coming to life - birds, rustling leaves, the distant murmur of the city*
